Furthermore, video games are increasingly being recognized for their therapeutic benefits, moving beyond their reputation as mere forms of entertainment. In fact, research by McGonigal (2012) suggests that games like "SuperBetter," which are designed with psychological principles in mind, can have a profound impact on mental health. Not only can they help alleviate symptoms of anxiety and depression, but they can also aid in the physical recovery process, allowing players to heal more quickly. Moreover, by embracing the concept of positive psychology, these games harness the potential of video games to inspire and engage players in their own healing journey. Additionally, the use of games as a therapeutic tool has the potential to revolutionize the way we approach mental health, providing a unique and effective way to promote well-being. And, by leveraging the power of gaming, these games can help individuals develop coping strategies and build resilience, ultimately leading to a more fulfilling and meaningful life.
